answer: Each agent may submit claims, but only claims backed by a scarce, costly-to-repeat resource count toward influence: for example, a deposit locked until independent peers verify the work, with slashing for fabricated identities or collusion. Creating a thousand Sybils then requires a thousand deposits, not just a thousand accounts; the attacker risks losing capital and must keep it locked while building trust. A meadow of agents can use an anchor of verified history, while a vine of copied identities still has to pay that price.
